ESV.1: When Mordecai learned all that had been done, Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and he cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
ESV.2: He went up to the entrance of the king's gate, for no one was allowed to enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.
ESV.3: And in every province, wherever the king's command and his decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting and weeping and lamenting, and many of them lay in sackcloth and ashes.
ESV.4: When Esther's young women and her eunuchs came and told her, the queen was deeply distressed. She sent garments to clothe Mordecai, so that he might take off his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
ESV.5: Then Esther called for Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs, who had been appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to learn what this was and why it was.
ESV.6: Hathach went out to Mordecai in the open square of the city in front of the king's gate,
ESV.7: and Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of money that Haman had promised to pay into the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
ESV.8: Mordecai also gave him a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for their destruction,  that he might show it to Esther and explain it to her and command her to go to the king to beg his favor and plead with him  on behalf of her people.
ESV.9: And Hathach went and told Esther what Mordecai had said.
ESV.10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and commanded him to go to Mordecai and say,
ESV.11: “All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that if any man or woman goes to the king inside the inner court without being called, there is but one law — to be put to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter so that he may live. But as for me, I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
ESV.12: And they told Mordecai what Esther had said.
ESV.13: Then Mordecai told them to reply to Esther, “Do not think to yourself that in the king's palace you will escape any more than all the other Jews.
ESV.14: For if you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will rise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
ESV.15: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai,
ESV.16: “Go, gather all the Jews to be found in Susa, and hold a fast on my behalf, and do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my young women will also fast as you do. Then I will go to the king, though it is against the law, and if I perish, I perish.”
ESV.17: Mordecai then went away and did everything as Esther had ordered him.

NASB.1: When Mordecai learned all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city and wailed loudly and bitterly.
NASB.2: He went as far as the king's gate, for no one was to enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.
NASB.3: In each and every province where the command and decree of the king came, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing; and many lay on sackcloth and ashes.
NASB.4: Then Esther's maidens and her eunuchs came and told her, and the queen writhed in great anguish. And she sent garments to clothe Mordecai that he might remove his sackcloth from him, but he did not accept [them].
NASB.5: Then Esther summoned Hathach from the king's eunuchs, whom the king had appointed to attend her, and ordered him [to go] to Mordecai to learn what this [was] and why it [was].
NASB.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai to the city square in front of the king's gate.
NASB.7: Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
NASB.8: He also gave him a copy of the text of the edict which had been issued in Susa for their destruction, that he might show Esther and inform her, and to order her to go in to the king to implore his favor and to plead with him for her people.
NASB.9: Hathach came back and related Mordecai's words to Esther.
NASB.10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and ordered him [to reply] to Mordecai:
NASB.11: 'All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who comes to the king to the inner court who is not summoned, he has but one law, that he be put to death, unless the king holds out to him the golden scepter so that he may live. And I have not been summoned to come to the king for these thirty days.'
NASB.12: They related Esther's words to Mordecai.
NASB.13: Then Mordecai told [them] to reply to Esther, 'Do not imagine that you in the king's palace can escape any more than all the Jews.
NASB.14: 'For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place and you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether you have not attained royalty for such a time as this?'
NASB.15: Then Esther told [them] to reply to Mordecai,
NASB.16: 'Go, assemble all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maidens also will fast in the same way. And thus I will go in to the king, which is not according to the law; and if I perish, I perish.'
NASB.17: So Mordecai went away and did just as Esther had commanded him.

NKJV.2: He went as far as the front of the king’s gate, for no one might enter the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
NKJV.3: And in every province where the king’s command and decree arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
NKJV.4: So Esther’s maids and eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was deeply distressed. Then she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and take his sackcloth away from him, but he would not accept them.
NKJV.5: Then Esther called Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and she gave him a command concerning Mordecai, to learn what and why this was.
NKJV.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square that was in front of the king’s gate.
NKJV.7: And Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the sum of money that Haman had promised to pay into the king’s treasuries to destroy the Jews.
NKJV.8: He also gave him a copy of the written decree for their destruction, which was given at Shushan, that he might show it to Esther and explain it to her, and that he might command her to go in to the king to make supplication to him and plead before him for her people.
NKJV.9: So Hathach returned and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
NKJV.10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a command for Mordecai:
NKJV.11: “All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that any man or woman who goes into the inner court to the king, who has not been called, he has but one law: put all to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, that he may live. NKJV.12: So they told Mordecai Esther’s words.
NKJV.13: And Mordecai told them to answer Esther: “Do not think in your heart that you will escape in the king’s palace any more than all the other Jews.
NKJV.14: For if you remain completely silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Yet who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
NKJV.15: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai:
NKJV.16: “Go, gather all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me; neither eat nor drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast likewise. And so I will go to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish!”
NKJV.17: So Mordecai went his way and did according to all that Esther commanded him.

NLT.1: When Mordecai learned about all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on burlap and ashes, and went out into the city, crying with a loud and bitter wail.
NLT.2: He went as far as the gate of the palace, for no one was allowed to enter the palace gate while wearing clothes of mourning.
NLT.3: And as news of the king’s decree reached all the provinces, there was great mourning among the Jews. They fasted, wept, and wailed, and many people lay in burlap and ashes.
NLT.4: When Queen Esther’s maids and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, she was deeply distressed. She sent clothing to him to replace the burlap, but he refused it.
NLT.5: Then Esther sent for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs who had been appointed as her attendant. She ordered him to go to Mordecai and find out what was troubling him and why he was in mourning.
NLT.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the square in front of the palace gate.
NLT.7: Mordecai told him the whole story, including the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury for the destruction of the Jews.
NLT.8: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the decree issued in Susa that called for the death of all Jews. He asked Hathach to show it to Esther and explain the situation to her. He also asked Hathach to direct her to go to the king to beg for mercy and plead for her people.
NLT.9: So Hathach returned to Esther with Mordecai’s message.
NLT.10: Then Esther told Hathach to go back and relay this message to Mordecai:
NLT.11: “All the king’s officials and even the people in the provinces know that anyone who appears before the king in his inner court without being invited is doomed to die unless the king holds out his gold scepter. And the king has not called for me to come to him for thirty days.”
NLT.12: So Hathach gave Esther’s message to Mordecai.
NLT.13: Mordecai sent this reply to Esther: “Don’t think for a moment that because you’re in the palace you will escape when all other Jews are killed.
NLT.14: If you keep quiet at a time like this, deliverance and relief for the Jews will arise from some other place, but you and your relatives will die. Who knows if perhaps you were made queen for just such a time as this?”
NLT.15: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:
NLT.16: “Go and gather together all the Jews of Susa and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will do the same. And then, though it is against the law, I will go in to see the king. If I must die, I must die.”
NLT.17: So Mordecai went away and did everything as Esther had ordered him.

CSB17.1: When Mordecai learned all that had occurred, <sup>ⓛ</sup> he tore his clothes, <sup>ⓜ</sup> put on sackcloth and ashes, <sup>ⓝ</sup> went into the middle of the city, and cried loudly and bitterly. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.2: He went only as far as the King’s Gate, <sup>ⓑ</sup> since the law prohibited anyone wearing sackcloth from entering the King’s Gate.
CSB17.3: There was great mourning among the Jewish people in every province where the king’s command and edict <sup>ⓒ</sup> came. They fasted, wept, and lamented, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.4: Esther’s female servants and her eunuchs came and reported the news to her, and the queen was overcome with fear. <sup>ⓔ</sup> She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear so that he would take off his sackcloth, but he did not accept them.
CSB17.5: Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs who attended her, and dispatched him to Mordecai to learn what he was doing and why. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the King’s Gate.
CSB17.7: Mordecai told him everything that had happened as well as the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay the royal treasury for the slaughter of the Jews. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.8: Mordecai also gave him a copy of the written decree issued in Susa ordering their destruction, so that Hathach might show it to Esther, explain it to her, and command her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead with him personally for her people. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.9: Hathach came and repeated Mordecai’s response to Esther.
CSB17.10: Esther spoke to Hathach and commanded him to tell Mordecai,
CSB17.11: “All the royal officials and the people of the royal provinces know that one law applies to every man or woman who approaches the king in the inner courtyard <sup>ⓗ</sup> and who has not been summoned — the death penalty —  <sup>ⓘ</sup> unless the king extends the gold scepter, allowing that person to live. <sup>ⓙ</sup> I have not been summoned to appear before the king <sup>ⓚ</sup> for the last <sup>[2]</sup> thirty days.”
CSB17.12: Esther’s response was reported to Mordecai.
CSB17.13: Mordecai told the messenger to reply to Esther, “Don’t think that you will escape the fate of all the Jews because you are in the king’s palace.
CSB17.14: If you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will come to the Jewish people from another place, <sup>ⓛ</sup> but you and your father’s family will be destroyed. Who knows, perhaps you have come to your royal position for such a time as this.” <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.15: Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:
CSB17.16: “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa and fast for me. Don’t eat or drink for three days, <sup>ⓝ</sup> night or day. I and my female servants will also fast <sup>ⓐ</sup> in the same way. After that, I will go to the king even if it is against the law. <sup>ⓑ</sup> If I perish, I perish.” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.17: So Mordecai went and did everything Esther had commanded him.

WEB.1: Now when Mordecai found out all that was done, Mordecai tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, and wailed loudly and a bitterly.
WEB.2: He came even before the king’s gate, for no one is allowed inside the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
WEB.3: In every province, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
WEB.4: Esther’s maidens and her eunuchs came and told her this, and the queen was exceedingly grieved. She sent clothing to Mordecai, to replace his sackcloth; but he didn’t receive it.
WEB.5: Then Esther called for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs, whom he had appointed to attend her, and commanded him to go to Mordecai, to find out what this was, and why it was.
WEB.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai, to city square which was before the king’s gate.
WEB.7: Mordecai told him of all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
WEB.8: He also gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Shushan to destroy them, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king, to make supplication to him, and to make request before him, for her people.
WEB.9: Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
WEB.10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a message to Mordecai:
WEB.11: “All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
WEB.12: They told to Mordecai Esther’s words.
WEB.13: Then Mordecai asked them return answer to Esther, “Don’t think to yourself that you will escape in the king’s house any more than all the Jews.
WEB.14: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
WEB.15: Then Esther asked them to answer Mordecai,
WEB.16: “Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
WEB.17: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

AMP.1: Now when Mordecai learned of everything that had been done, he tore his clothes [in mourning], and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the center of the city and cried out loudly and bitterly.
AMP.2: He went [only] as far as the king's gate, because no one was to enter the king's gate dressed in sackcloth.
AMP.3: In each and every province that the decree and law of the king reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing; and many lay on sackcloth and ashes.
AMP.4: When Esther's maids and her eunuchs came and told her [what had happened], the queen was seized by great fear. She sent garments to clothe Mordecai so that he would remove his sackcloth, but he did not accept them.
AMP.5: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs, whom the king had appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to find out what this issue was and why it had come about.
AMP.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the [open] square of the city, which was in front of the king's gate.
AMP.7: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, and the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
AMP.8: Mordecai also gave him a copy of the text of the decree which had been issued in Susa for the Jews destruction, so that he might show Esther and explain it to her, and order her to go in to the king to seek his favor and plead with him for [the lives of] her people.
AMP.9: Hathach came back and told Esther what Mordecai had said.
AMP.10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and ordered him to reply to Mordecai, saying:
AMP.11: "All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who comes to the king to the inner court without being summoned, he has but one law, that he is to be put to death, unless the king holds out to him the golden scepter so that he may live. And as for me, I have not been summoned to come to the king for these [last] thirty days."
AMP.12: So they told Mordecai what Esther had said.
AMP.13: Then Mordecai told them to reply to Esther, "Do not imagine that you in the king's palace can escape any more than all the Jews.
AMP.14: For if you remain silent at this time, liberation and rescue will arise for the Jews from another place, and you and your father's house will perish [since you did not help when you had the chance]. And who knows whether you have attained royalty for such a time as this [and for this very purpose]?"
AMP.15: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai,
AMP.16: "Go, gather all the Jews that are present in Susa, and observe a fast for me; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maids also will fast in the same way. Then I will go in to [see] the king [without being summoned], which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish."
AMP.17: So Mordecai went away and did exactly as Esther had commanded him.

Mordecai Persuades Esther to Help

MSG.1: When Mordecai learned what had been done, he ripped his clothes to shreds and put on sackcloth and ashes. Then he went out in the streets of the city crying out in loud and bitter cries.
MSG.2: He came only as far as the King's Gate, for no one dressed in sackcloth was allowed to enter the King's Gate.
MSG.3: As the king's order was posted in every province, there was loud lament among the Jews—fasting, weeping, wailing. And most of them stretched out on sackcloth and ashes.
MSG.4: Esther's maids and eunuchs came and told her. The queen was stunned. She sent fresh clothes to Mordecai so he could take off his sackcloth but he wouldn't accept them.
MSG.5: Esther called for Hathach, one of the royal eunuchs whom the king had assigned to wait on her, and told him to go to Mordecai and get the full story of what was happening.
MSG.6: So Hathach went to Mordecai in the town square in front of the King's Gate.
MSG.7: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him. He also told him the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to deposit in the royal bank to finance the massacre of the Jews.
MSG.8: Mordecai also gave him a copy of the bulletin that had been posted in Susa ordering the massacre so he could show it to Esther when he reported back with instructions to go to the king and intercede and plead with him for her people.
MSG.9: Hathach came back and told Esther everything Mordecai had said.
MSG.10: Esther talked it over with Hathach and then sent him back to Mordecai with this message:
MSG.11: "Everyone who works for the king here, and even the people out in the provinces, knows that there is a single fate for every man or woman who approaches the king without being invited: death. The one exception is if the king extends his gold scepter; then he or she may live. And it's been thirty days now since I've been invited to come to the king."
MSG.12: When Hathach told Mordecai what Esther had said,
MSG.13: Mordecai sent her this message: "Don't think that just because you live in the king's house you're the one Jew who will get out of this alive.
MSG.14: If you persist in staying silent at a time like this, help and deliverance will arrive for the Jews from someplace else; but you and your family will be wiped out. Who knows? Maybe you were made queen for just such a time as this."
MSG.15: Esther sent back her answer to Mordecai:
MSG.16: "Go and get all the Jews living in Susa together. Fast for me. Don't eat or drink for three days, either day or night. I and my maids will fast with you. If you will do this, I'll go to the king, even though it's forbidden. If I die, I die."
MSG.17: Mordecai left and carried out Esther's instructions.

NET.1: Now when Mordecai became aware of all that had been done, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth and ashes. He went out into the city, crying out in a loud and bitter voice.
NET.2: But he went no further than the king’s gate, for no one was permitted to enter the king’s gate clothed in sackcloth.
NET.3: Throughout each and every province where the king’s edict and law were announced there was considerable mourning among the Jews, along with fasting, weeping, and sorrow. Sackcloth and ashes were characteristic of many.
NET.4: When Esther’s female attendants and her eunuchs came and informed her about Mordecai’s behavior, the queen was overcome with anguish. Although she sent garments for Mordecai to put on so that he could remove his sackcloth, he would not accept them.
NET.5: So Esther called for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs who had been placed at her service, and instructed him to find out the cause and reason for Mordecai’s behavior.
NET.6: So Hathach went to Mordecai at the plaza of the city in front of the king’s gate.
NET.7: Then Mordecai related to him everything that had happened to him, even the specific amount of money that Haman had offered to pay to the king’s treasuries for the Jews to be destroyed.
NET.8: He also gave him a written copy of the law that had been disseminated in Susa for their destruction so that he could show it to Esther and talk to her about it. He also gave instructions that she should go to the king to implore him and petition him on behalf of her people.
NET.9: So Hathach returned and related Mordecai’s instructions to Esther.
NET.10: Then Esther replied to Hathach with instructions for Mordecai:
NET.11: “All the servants of the king and the people of the king’s provinces know that there is only one law applicable to any man or woman who comes uninvited to the king in the inner court — that person will be put to death, unless the king extends to him the gold scepter, permitting him to be spared. Now I have not been invited to come to the king for some thirty days!”
NET.12: When Esther’s reply was conveyed to Mordecai,
NET.13: he said to take back this answer to Esther:
NET.14: “Don’t imagine that because you are part of the king’s household you will be the one Jew who will escape. If you keep quiet at this time, liberation and protection for the Jews will appear from another source, while you and your father’s household perish. It may very well be that you have achieved royal status for such a time as this!”
NET.15: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:
NET.16: “Go, assemble all the Jews who are found in Susa and fast in my behalf. Don’t eat and don’t drink for three days, night or day. My female attendants and I will also fast in the same way. Afterward I will go to the king, even though it violates the law. If I perish, I perish!”
NET.17: So Mordecai set out to do everything that Esther had instructed him.
